name: Reflex Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Reflex Epilepsy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Seizures are consistently and exclusively triggered by specific stimuli or activities
Electroencephalogram (EEG) shows epileptiform discharges time-locked to the triggering stimulus
Exclusion of other epilepsy syndromes without reflex triggers
Detailed clinical history confirming reproducible seizure induction by specific stimuli

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of seizures consistently triggered by specific stimuli with EEG confirmation of epileptiform activity time-locked to the stimulus and exclusion of other epilepsy syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Triggers may include visual stimuli, reading, startle, or somatosensory stimuli.

pathognomonic.notes: Seizures occur immediately or shortly after exposure to specific triggers
Epileptiform discharges elicited by photic stimulation on EEG

common.notes: Frequently triggered by visual stimuli such as flashing lights

common.symptomName: Myoclonic jerks triggered by sudden stimuli
searchTerms: quick muscle jerks after sudden events

common.notes: May be triggered by specific cognitive or sensory stimuli
Subjective sensory or experiential phenomena before seizure onset

occasional.notes: Transient visual disturbances triggered by stimuli
searchTerms: seeing lights or shapes without convulsions

occasional.notes: Includes pallor, sweating, or gastrointestinal sensations
searchTerms: seizure symptoms affecting automatic body functions
changes in heart rate or sweating with seizures

occasional.notes: Sensitivity to light that may precede seizures

rare.notes: Prolonged or repeated seizures induced by triggers
searchTerms: status epilepticus caused by reflex triggers

rare.symptomName: Psychogenic non-epileptic seizures mimicking reflex epilepsy

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of seizures
imaging: Normal brain MRI in most cases
Occasional focal cortical dysplasia or structural abnormalities in some patients
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with photosensitive epilepsy (e.g., CHD2, GABRA1) in some cases
other: EEG demonstrating epileptiform discharges time-locked to specific stimuli
Video-EEG monitoring to capture reflex seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Seizures triggered specifically by photic stimuli
Myoclonic seizures typically occur on awakening
Seizures not consistently triggered by specific stimuli

redFlags: Seizures unresponsive to standard antiepileptic drugs
Prolonged seizures or status epilepticus triggered by stimuli
Presence of focal neurological deficits or progressive neurological decline
references: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification and Diagnostic Criteria for Reflex Epilepsies, 2022
Fisher RS, et al. Epileptic seizures and epilepsy: definitions proposed by the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) and the International Bureau for Epilepsy (IBE). Epilepsia. 2014
Panayiotopoulos CP. Reflex epilepsies and reflex seizures. Epilepsia. 2005
